title: The Gift That Was Difficult to Accept
title_ja: 受け取りにくかった贈り物
fact_notes: 人物・制度・具体的な出来事は架空の教材例・思考実験。実在の調査・統計・法令・実証結果を示すものではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: In a fictional story, two friends named Hana and Lina were preparing to celebrate the anniversary of the day they had first met.
sentences.ja: 架空の物語でハナとリナという友人二人は初めて出会った日の記念日を祝う準備をしていた。

sentences.en: Lina had saved money for several months and purchased an expensive concert ticket that she intended to give to Hana as a surprise.
sentences.ja: リナは数カ月貯金し、ハナにサプライズとして贈るつもりで高価なコンサート券を購入した。

sentences.en: Hana appreciated the thought behind the gift but became worried when she discovered how much it had cost.
sentences.ja: ハナは贈り物に込められた気持ちに感謝したが、値段を知って心配になった。

sentences.en: She had been planning to make a small handmade present and wondered whether her own gift would appear inadequate by comparison.
sentences.ja: 小さな手作りの贈り物を用意する予定で、自分の贈り物が比較して不十分に見えるのではないかと考えた。

sentences.en: Initially, Hana considered using most of her remaining savings to purchase a more expensive present without explaining her concern to Lina.
sentences.ja: 当初ハナは心配をリナに説明せず残りの貯金の大半でより高価な贈り物を買うことを考えた。

sentences.en: However, she realized that this decision would leave her with little money for other activities that she had already planned.
sentences.ja: しかしこの決定では既に予定していた他の活動に使えるお金がほとんど残らないと気づいた。

sentences.en: Lina had never suggested that she expected an equally valuable object in return, so Hana questioned whether her sense of obligation reflected an actual agreement.
sentences.ja: リナは同じ価値の品をお返しに期待するとは一度も示していなかったため、ハナは義務感が実際の合意を反映するのか疑問に思った。

sentences.en: Rather than trying to guess what her friend expected, she decided to explain why she felt uncomfortable accepting the ticket.
sentences.ja: 友人の期待を推測するのでなく、券を受け取ることに抵抗を感じる理由を説明することにした。

sentences.en: During their conversation, Lina explained that she had chosen the concert because the two friends had often talked about the musician together.
sentences.ja: 会話でリナは二人がよくその音楽家について話していたのでコンサートを選んだと説明した。

sentences.en: She had regarded the ticket as an opportunity to share a meaningful experience rather than as the beginning of an exchange involving objects of equal financial value.
sentences.ja: 券を同じ金銭的価値の品の交換の始まりでなく、意味ある体験を共有する機会と考えていた。

sentences.en: She also understood that a well-intentioned surprise could create pressure when the recipient had not been able to discuss the arrangement beforehand.
sentences.ja: 善意のサプライズでも受け手が事前に話し合えなければ負担になり得ると理解した。

sentences.en: The friends agreed that future plans involving substantial expenses should be discussed together before either person made a purchase.
sentences.ja: 大きな費用を伴う今後の計画は購入前に話し合うことにした。

sentences.en: Hana eventually accepted the ticket after confirming that Lina was comfortable with the arrangement and did not expect financial repayment.
sentences.ja: リナが取り決めに納得し金銭的見返りを期待していないことを確認して、ハナは最終的に券を受け取った。

sentences.en: She gave Lina the handmade present that she had originally intended to prepare and included a letter explaining the memories that had inspired it.
sentences.ja: 当初用意するつもりだった手作り品を贈り、そのきっかけの思い出を説明する手紙も添えた。

sentences.en: Neither friend attempted to calculate whether the two presents represented exactly the same amount of effort or affection.
sentences.ja: どちらも二つの贈り物が全く同じ量の努力や愛情を表すか計算しようとしなかった。

sentences.en: Instead, they considered whether their choices were freely made and whether each person understood the meaning intended by the other.
sentences.ja: 代わりに選択が自由になされ、互いの意図した意味を理解しているか考えた。

sentences.en: This story illustrates that generosity can become complicated when an act of kindness creates an obligation that the giver did not intend.
sentences.ja: この物語は親切な行為が贈り手の意図しない義務を生むと寛大さが複雑になり得ることを示す。

sentences.en: The financial value of a gift may be relevant to a person's circumstances without providing a complete measure of the relationship itself.
sentences.ja: 贈り物の金銭的価値は個人の事情に関係しても、関係自体の完全な尺度にはならない。

sentences.en: Open communication can help friends distinguish freely chosen generosity from expectations that have never been explicitly agreed upon.
sentences.ja: 率直な対話は自由に選んだ親切と明示的に合意したことのない期待を区別する助けになる。

sentences.en: For Hana and Lina, a meaningful celebration required understanding each other's circumstances rather than attempting to make their gifts financially identical.
sentences.ja: 二人にとって意味ある祝いには贈り物の金額を同じにしようとするのでなく互いの事情を理解する必要があった。

questions.prompt: Why did Hana worry about her own gift?
options: She had promised to buy the same ticket.
Its apparent financial value was much lower.
questions.explanation_ja: 金銭的な差を心配した。

questions.prompt: What did Hana consider doing first?
options: Spending much of her savings on a more expensive present.
Asking Lina to pay for other activities.
questions.explanation_ja: 貯金を使い高価な品を買う案。

options: That she was expected to return a gift of equal monetary value.
That the ticket had been purchased.
questions.explanation_ja: 同額のお返しが必要という想定。

questions.prompt: Why had Lina chosen the concert?
options: She intended to test Hana's income.
They had often discussed the musician together.
She wanted a more expensive gift in return.

questions.prompt: What did Lina recognize about surprises?
options: A surprise always creates an explicit agreement.
A kind intention does not prevent a recipient from feeling pressured.
questions.explanation_ja: 善意でも圧力になる場合。

questions.prompt: What did Hana ultimately give Lina?
options: A handmade present and a letter.
A ticket of exactly equal price.
A receipt for a future repayment.

questions.prompt: What did the friends use instead of comparing gift prices?
options: A formula equating money and affection.
The average price of presents among friends.
A fixed rule for all celebrations.
Whether the choices were freely made and intentions understood.
questions.explanation_ja: 自由な選択と意図の理解。

questions.prompt: Which statement best reflects the story?
options: Every gift should be matched by an equal purchase.
Generosity can be meaningful without equal spending when expectations and circumstances are understood.
questions.explanation_ja: 金額の一致より事情と期待の理解。
